checks.finding: REQ-004 says override values equal to the record baseline must be rejected, and AC-031 requires that no-op case to be tested, but the spec defines credential_bearing and release_write as override-only names without defining their baseline values or where those values come from (requirements.md:77-98; acceptance-tests.md:36-37). Implementers cannot determine which values are no-ops or build the required fixture consistently. This is a Phase-1 behavior contract gap that would force design or implementation authors to invent the validation rule; Major because it blocks a deterministic schema and test oracle.

No direct conflict found between the stated Phase-1 and Phase-2 tuples or their acceptance oracles: REQ-001 and AC-001 specify full/legacy-seven-layer/advisory, while REQ-008 and AC-014–015 specify the atomic full/facet-hybrid/required transition and reject partial transitions (requirements.md:35-44,137-145,218-232).

The material negative and boundary cases have observable planned oracles, including missing/overlapping/unowned paths, stale evidence, invalid rollback approvals, changed approver cardinality, missing promotion evidence, and zero-friction recording (requirements.md:292-301; acceptance-tests.md:18-24,35-40,95-103,114-122). They remain planned, as appropriate for Phase 1.

The mutable A1–A8 availability assumption is explicitly deferred to a current-HEAD preflight that blocks on missing or incompatible dependencies, with a corresponding observable criterion (requirements.md:167-174,311-319; acceptance-tests.md:26-27,32). OQ-001–OQ-006 are recorded as resolved, and unresolved dependency state is not silently assumed.

Human approval and protected publication boundaries are explicit and testable: Context publication rejects missing or invalid approval binding, agents cannot approve protected records or WFIs, and rollback requires the applicable distinct-approval or signed cooldown path (requirements.md:37-44,147-165,273-279; acceptance-tests.md:7-8,22-25).

The undefined baseline for the two override-only characteristics leaves the REQ-004 rejection rule and AC-031 no-op oracle unresolved (requirements.md:77-98; acceptance-tests.md:36-37). Implementation-policy review cannot assess a deterministic schema contract or test expectation without inventing that behavior, so this Phase-1 specification is not ready for handoff.
